I didn't want to log in twice, so I edited the URL on the 2020 bug: https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/avatar-shakingjittering-with-oculus-steamvr

In the mean time I an curious which is better. Is it better to use Oculus VRChat with go go loco, or better to suffer jitter with the ovrtoolkit?

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name}: For me answer is only one: suffer with jitter but using Gogo loco and ovrtoolkit at this same time. For me, combo of this two stuff is must have. But i want to have ovrtoolkit on oculus store or build features from him into vrc, this is my solution.

details:
1.Go on Oculus store, play VRC a front of mirror=Everything perfect, after go under 45fps

2.Go on SteamVR, play VRC a front of mirror=You will see a jitter/shaking, face, hairs (most) and hands (completely mostly), doesn't matter what avatar i pick, disable AWS, or make a resolution as potato.

I noticed in one of the posts how you say it is fixed by Valve, but no, I have my headset since 2018 and this problem still exists in VRChat

Because of this shaking, many rooms are unplayable because my whole avatar is shaking, hands too, on oculus software, the hand shaking is still there but not like on SteamVR, on SteamVR it's a nightmare.

I can't use the Oculus Version because I use OVRToolKit to change the height to sit smoothly on the floor etc. (I have health issues with my legs to play VRChat in a standing position, I can only play from a seated position)

This would be good to give us the option to smoothly change height when we press the analogue and move our hand as in the OVR in the VRChat itself, if you don't know how to fix this, or can't tell Valve to fix this problem. This way we can use the Oculus software and still have the same features as on SteamVR. 

Please developers, hear my voice, because I spend a lot of time in VRChat, I love this community app, my friends and a lot of heart in all stuff made by community, but after playing for a long time in real life I can feel my hands and eyes shaking like in the app, I think it doesn't sound right.

There are still a lot of CV1 gamers out there because they are used cheaply and create a doorway for more VR gamers.

There still a lot of players with CV1, because used one are cheap and making a door for more VR Players.
